title: Reconnaissance Marine, Parachute and Combatant Diver Qualified (MGySgt to Pvt) NMOS (0321), DC PP&O
raw_text:
10. MOS 0326, Reconnaissance Marine, Parachute and Combatant Diver Qualified
(MGySgt to Pvt) NMOS (0321), DC PP&O

    a. Summary. Reconnaissance Marine, Parachute and Combatant Diver
Qualified, conduct airborne and subsurface operations to clandestinely gain
access to the operating environment to conduct full-spectrum amphibious



                                         3-30                        Enclosure (1)
 3110                                                                 NAVMC 1200.1L



reconnaissance, ground reconnaissance & surveillance, preparation of the
operational environment and shaping, and specialized raid missions in support
of the division, MEF, other MAGTFs, or joint force.

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Must hold MOS 0321, Reconnaissance Marine.

        (2) Must have current Physically Qualified (PQ) Naval Special
Warfare/Special Operations Physical to perform combatant diver and HALO/ HAHO
duties in accordance with inter-service requirements established in reference
(ai) and Standards of Medical Fitness.

        (3) Must have passed the USSOCOM in test and the physical screening
test in accordance with USSOCOM Manual 350-4V1 and MILPERSMAN 1220-410 (Seal/
EOD/SWCC/Diver/Air Physical Screening Testing Standards and Procedures)
within 30 days before Combatant Diver Course (N20L6H1) attendance.

       c.   Requirements

            (1) Must complete the Basic Airborne Course (A030CG1).

            (2) Must complete the Multi Mission Parachute Course (M50KLD1).

            (3) Must complete the Combatant Diver Qualification Course (N20L6H1).

            (4) Maintain physical fitness standards specified by COMNAVMEDCOM.

    d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to
reference (ca), the Reconnaissance Training and Readiness Manual.

    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
Special Forces 55-3018.

       f.   Related Military Skill

            (1) Rifleman, 0311.

            (2) Reconnaissance Marine, 0321.

            (3) Reconnaissance Marine, Sniper Qualified, 0322.

            (4) Reconnaissance Marine, Parachute Qualified, 0323.

            (5) Reconnaissance Marine, Combatant Diver Qualified, 0324.

            (6) Marine Raider, 0372.

            (7) Combat Rubber Reconnaissance Craft Coxswain, 8020.
common_text: In addition to the Infantry Officer, Marine Gunner, and Infantry Unit Leader, the 03 Infantry Occupational Field is comprised of the following specialties rifleman, light armor vehicle marine, reconnaissance marine, machine gunner, mortarman, and antitank missile gunner. Regardless of specialty, Infantry Marines are primarily employed in units from the team to regimental-level in order to locate, close with, and destroy the enemy in all environments and weather conditions, during both the day and night. Excluding Light Armored Reconnaissance Units, Infantry Marines are principally trained to operate light and fast on foot. Infantry units are capable of multiple methods of entry and insertion, embarking aboard and fighting from helicopters, assault amphibious vehicles, motorized tactical vehicles, ultra-light tactical vehicles, and small boats. As the principal component of a Marine Air-Ground Task Force's ground combat element, Infantry Marines must be able to operate effectively in austere and distributed environments characterized by friction, uncertainty, and chaos. All Infantry Marines must be physically dominant and masters of small arms marksmanship, tactical combat casualty care, and battle drills in every operating environment. Infantry units must be comprised of Marines proficient in the employment of demolitions, rockets, machineguns, mortars, and missile systems and capable of directing supporting arms. Infantry Marines must also be proficient in field craft and capable of employing unmanned systems, limited information warfare, and non-lethal systems.

In addition to the Infantry Officer, Marine Gunner, and Infantry Unit Leader, the 03 Infantry Occupational Field is comprised of the following specialties rifleman, light armor vehicle marine, reconnaissance marine, machine gunner, mortarman, and antitank missile gunner. Regardless of specialty, Infantry Marines are primarily employed in units from the team to regimental-level in order to locate, close with, and destroy the enemy in all environments and weather conditions, during both the day and night. Excluding Light Armored Reconnaissance Units, Infantry Marines are principally trained to operate light and fast on foot. Infantry units are capable of multiple methods of entry and insertion, embarking aboard and fighting from helicopters, assault amphibious vehicles, motorized tactical vehicles, ultra-light tactical vehicles, and small boats. As the principal component of a Marine Air-Ground Task Force's ground combat element, Infantry Marines must be able to operate effectively in austere and distributed environments characterized by friction, uncertainty, and chaos. All Infantry Marines must be physically dominant and masters of small arms marksmanship, tactical combat casualty care, and battle drills in every operating environment. Infantry units must be comprised of Marines proficient in the employment of demolitions, rockets, machineguns, mortars, and missile systems and capable of directing supporting arms. Infantry Marines must also be proficient in field craft and capable of employing unmanned systems, limited information warfare, and non-lethal systems.

Reconnaissance Marine, Parachute and Combatant Diver Qualified, conduct airborne and subsurface operations to clandestinely gain access to the operating environment to conduct full-spectrum amphibious reconnaissance, ground reconnaissance & surveillance, preparation of the operational environment and shaping, and specialized raid missions in support of the division, MEF, other MAGTFs, or joint force. b. Prerequisites (1) Must hold MOS 0321, Reconnaissance Marine. (2) Must have current Physically Qualified (PQ) Naval Special Warfare/Special Operations Physical to perform combatant diver and HALO/ HAHO duties in accordance with inter-service requirements established in reference (ai) and Standards of Medical Fitness. (3) Must have passed the USSOCOM in test and the physical screening test in accordance with USSOCOM Manual 350-4V1 and MILPERSMAN 1220-410 (Seal/ EOD/SWCC/Diver/Air Physical Screening Testing Standards and Procedures) within 30 days before Combatant Diver Course (N20L6H1) attendance. c. Requirements (1) Must complete the Basic Airborne Course (A030CG1). (2) Must complete the Multi Mission Parachute Course (M50KLD1). (3) Must complete the Combatant Diver Qualification Course (N20L6H1). (4) Maintain physical fitness standards specified by COMNAVMEDCOM. d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to reference (ca), the Reconnaissance Training and Readiness Manual.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
